depiction.primary_object: Circular arrow curving counter-clockwise pointing left at the top

readings.meaning: reset or restore to previous state
return or send back an item

ambiguity: Easy to confuse with clockwise refresh/reload arrows, replay buttons, or general recurring task indicators.

example_tasks.task: Roll back the broken billing migration on production before Monday morning
Restore MacBook from last Tuesday's Time Machine snapshot
Reset the garage keypad code after the painters finish up
Reverse the accidental duplicate transfer to savings account
Check if refund hit the card
Test the snapshot on staging first
Revert the living room DNS settings back to automatic on the router
Send back the wrong-sized radiator valves to Screwfix before the 30-day window closes
Undo the bulk permission changes on the shared client Google Drive folder
Reset the service interval light on the Honda dashboard after changing the oil

example_tasks_es: Restablecer de fábrica el móvil viejo antes de venderlo
Devolver los pantalones de Zara que me quedan grandes
Revertir los cambios en la plantilla de presupuesto

Сбросить настройки старого телефона до заводских

context_tasks.task: Pack up the faulty espresso machine in its original box for return
Write post-mortem note on why we had to roll back release 2.4

Paperclip inside the recess for 10 seconds to reset the smart bridge

reasoning: A counter-clockwise circular arrow is the standard UI glyph for undo, reset, revert, or roll back, and secondarily serves for merchandise returns. While mostly an abstract action or UI chrome, it genuinely fits tech rollback/reset tasks and shopping returns when no specific object icon applies, though it is easily confused with clockwise refresh or repeat arrows.
